question: Which of the following is absent in prokaryotic cells?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuclear membrane.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Prokaryotic cells are the cells that lack a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
 
• These cells have a single, circular chromosome that floats freely in the cytoplasm.
 
• Prokaryotic cells are usually smaller in size than eukaryotic cells and are found in bacteria and archaea.
 
• The absence of a nuclear membrane in prokaryotic cells enables them to replicate faster than eukaryotic cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cheek cells are eukaryotic cells that contain a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

 
 
• These cells are obtained from the inner lining of the cheek and are commonly used for DNA analysis.
 
 
 
• Eukaryotic cells are cells that contain a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
• These cells are found in plants, animals, fungi, and protists.
 
 
 
• Onion cells are eukaryotic cells that are commonly used in biology labs for studying cell division and cell structure.
 
 
• These cells contain a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
